## Exchanging a PAT for an ISC Access Token

Use the **OAuth2 client credentials grant** against your tenant's `/oauth/token` endpoint. The credentials go in the **POST body** — never in the URL query string.

### Request

```http
POST https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

grant_type=client_credentials&client_id={your_client_id}&client_secret={your_client_secret}
```

Replace `{tenant}` with your ISC tenant name (e.g. `acme` → `https://acme.api.identitynow.com`).

### curl example

```bash
curl -X POST "https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/oauth/token" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --data-urlencode "grant_type=client_credentials" \
  --data-urlencode "client_id={your_client_id}" \
  --data-urlencode "client_secret={your_client_secret}"
```

### Response

```json
{
  "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5...",
  "token_type": "Bearer",
  "expires_in": 750
}
```

### Using the token

Pass it as a bearer token on every subsequent API call:

```http
GET https://{tenant}.api.identitynow.com/v3/accounts
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5...
```

> **Note for beta endpoints:** also add the header `X-SailPoint-Experimental: true`.

### Key notes

- Rate limit is **100 requests per token per 10 seconds**. If you get a `429`, respect the `Retry-After` response header.
- You can have at most **10 PATs per user** in ISC.

---

  - method: POST
    path: /oauth/token
    api_version: oauth
auth_flow: OAuth2 client credentials grant
required_scopes: []
key_parameters: [grant_type, client_id, client_secret]
```
